scoreExplanation.shapeVolume: Rounded continuous rim and deliberately recessed face replace the old hard polygonal slab; relief remains attached and legible through every authored turn.
scoreExplanation.color: Orange-gold edge depth, yellow face and darker bar now separate at compact game size. Saturated gold identity is retained.
scoreExplanation.lightingHighlights: Broad warm edge rolloff reveals thickness without a white glare sheet, a black lower edge or a preferred horizontal key.
scoreExplanation.materialDetail: Dimensional star glints and crafted rim/face/bar construction provide useful detail without text/noise.
scoreExplanation.artifactFreeReadability: All48 frames show a coherent rise/grow/turn/shrink. The bar and coin remain recognizable at64px/cell; tiny endpoint and late faded details are intentionally low-visibility. No material dead spot, clipping, seam, halo or flicker found.

observations: The candidate visibly advances the original toward the fixed target: its rim is round and substantial, the inset reads as a distinct coin face, and the raised bar has a small highlight plus darker body rather than merging into a flat bright yellow disc.

Gold midtones and warm orange side shading retain the source palette while giving the continuous rounded edge a softer cartoon finish. The brightest bands remain contained within the geometry and leave the face/bar readable.

Clean dimensional four-point glints replace the old plus beams. The three small sparkles stay coherent with the coin, with no unrelated prop or amount text. Their old construction and part count were correctly treated as design freedom.

Across all four native facings and12 phases, the silhouette stays compact, the currency relief does not detach or disappear midclip, and the start/end collapse remains intentional. All four directions are pixel-identical, as appropriate for this camera-facing effect.

The actual Godot fixture shows the established short reward effect at the existing customer ground root with the unchanged .9s fade on three backgrounds and two scales. Its brief overlap with the customer is inherited from the frozen registration policy and is not a newly introduced offset or grounds for moving it.

The native model, camera and all48 independent recaptures are consistent with the supplied sprites. The visible improvement is achieved with dimensional editable meshes and native materials, not a target image plane or final-pixel manipulation.
remainingDifferences: The candidate uses a smoothly rounded turned rim rather than the target’s more angular/chamfered outer edge and sharper polished streaks; the softer treatment fits the chosen cartoon finish.
The native gold is more softly diffuse and less mirror-like than the ImageGen target. This preserves readable midtones and avoids copying its preferred-side glare.

It retains three original-role glints instead of the target’s four and does not enlarge the object to match the target’s normalized silhouette. Spark count is nonfunctional, and the compact registered scale is deliberately preserved.
Late runtime frames naturally become faint under the frozen alpha fade, and first/last native phases are nearly vanished. Those phase semantics are intentional, not missing imagery.

technicalEvidence.result: All independent frozen-contract checks pass. No material visual blockers remain.

No preferred horizontal lighting or directional ground cast shadow.
